inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q weighted-average DILUTED shares (906M, quarter ended 2026-06-30). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it. UNH is a repurchaser (FY2025 $5.5B, H1 2026 $1.6B after a Q1 2026 pause), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation, $971M). Tax withheld on net-share settlement is not separately tagged in XBRL (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent); UNH SBC is ~0.2% of revenue so the omission is immaterial (<$1/share).
inputs.interest_income_basis: UNH reports $3,920M FY2025 investment and other income inside revenue/operating earnings, earned on ~$89B of cash plus short- and long-term investments. The ~$61B investment portfolio backs medical costs payable ($38.9B) and statutory capital, so it is operating float: its income stays in the flows and it is NOT in the bridge. The $28.6B of cash & equivalents IS credited in net debt, so the share of investment income it earns (~30% of $3.92B ~= $1.2B) is stripped from last_fcf and the EBITDA margin paths are set ~0.25pp below reported (ex cash yield).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free 4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.9 (above UNH's long-run ~0.6 to reflect 2025-26 idiosyncratic volatility, but no ad-hoc premium) -> CoE ~8.8%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.0%; market-value weights ~82/18 (market cap ~$337B vs $73B debt) -> WACC ~8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: DOJ, MA-coding and execution risk are charged in the bear flows and the weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: US GAAP operating-lease cost (~$1.6B FY2025) is already inside operating costs, so EBITDA is post-lease; operating lease liabilities ($4.6B) are excluded from total_debt. One treatment, no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). NCI charged once in the bridge: FY2025 NI to NCI $751M (H1 2026 $387M); book NCI $6.07B + redeemable NCI $1.44B = $7.5B; bridge deducts $9.0B (~12x attributable NCI earnings, above book).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'). UNH is a managed-care insurer plus Optum services, but not a BVPS-compounder: equity is dominated by $110.6B goodwill, ROE pre-crisis ran 20-25%, claims are short-tail (payable within months) so OCF tracks net income closely, and value is earnings power. The owner-FCF engine with the regulated-float adjustment above (investment portfolio as operating, cash credited and its yield stripped) is the appropriate fit; the BVPS row is for book compounders like FRFHF. TROUGH FRAMING: FY2025 (operating margin 4.2%, EBITDA margin 5.2%) is a trough in the middle of the window, not a base rate. Mid-cycle margin is anchored on FY2017-FY2023 (EBITDA margin 8.7-9.8% incl. investment income, ~9.3% avg ex-COVID-2020), haircut ~1pp for structural V28 risk-adjustment, MA coding scrutiny and Optum Health shrinkage -> base mature EBITDA margin 7.8% ex cash yield (~8.05% reported). FY2026 (year 1) is ~75% observable: H1 2026 EBITDA margin 8.5%, but managed care H2 is seasonally weaker and the raised FY2026 adj EPS guide of $19.50-$20.00 implies a full-year EBITDA margin ~6.8-7.0% reported, hence year-1 base 6.75% ex cash yield. FY2025 is excluded from the margin base rate; historical CAGRs are reported both with and ex FY2025. A 10-year horizon is used because the margin is still recovering through year 4. Buybacks: repurchaser, flat count funded. Legal: $3.0B expected-value deduction for Change Healthcare MDL and a DOJ civil resolution in the bridge; a structural MA-coding regime change is the bear flow path, not a second fine.
inputs.price_volatility_note: Regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

equity_bridge.item: Noncontrolling interests (book $6.07B + redeemable $1.44B; valued ~12x $750M NCI earnings)
Expected legal resolution: Change Healthcare MDL + DOJ civil MA billing (probability-weighted)
equity_bridge.note: No reserve disclosed; MDL fact discovery closes Nov-2026, no trial date; DOJ criminal/civil probe expanded to Optum Rx in 2026. Judgment estimate, not a filing figure.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 7.9% diverges >30% from revenue 5y 11.7% and EPS 5y -3.9%. Every trailing CAGR ending FY2025 is distorted by the trough (EPS and FCF negative) and revenue is inflated by acquisitions (Change Healthcare, LHC, Amedisys-type deals) and MA share gains that UNH is now reversing. Not used mechanically: forward revenue growth is set from health-spend growth (~5-7% nominal) and the 2026 repricing, not from any trailing CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = FCF - SBC (cash-yield strip applied to FY0 only; historical cash/investment split not available in the series, effect on CAGRs is minor). Owner-FCF CAGR is slightly below reported FCF CAGR because SBC fell less than FCF in the trough, not because SBC is running away (SBC ~0.2-0.3% of revenue throughout). Ex-trough (FY2019-FY2023) the business compounded revenue, EPS and owner FCF at 11-13%; the base case does not assume that returns.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 ~flat (+0.5%): H1 2026 revenue +1.2% YoY with 965k fewer MA seniors and ~700k fewer Optum Health VBC patients. Re-accelerates to health-spend-plus growth (6.5%) as repricing completes and Optum Rx grows, fading to 3.5% by year 10.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Ex cash yield. Year 1 per raised FY2026 guide; recovers to 7.8% (reported ~8.05%, operating margin ~7.1%) by FY2029 -- ~1.2pp below the FY2017-23 mid-cycle for V28/coding/PBM structural drag. Implied GAAP EPS ~$23.5 FY2027 and ~$26 FY2028, i.e. the 13-16% algorithm for the two recovery years only, then health-spend growth.
base.cash_tax_rationale: FY2025 GAAP ETR 12.9% was one-off; FY2018-24 ETR 20.5-24.1%, H1 2026 18.6%. Unlevered cash rate ramps 20% -> 22%.
base.wc_rationale: Positive but small: medical costs payable (~8.7% of revenue) grows with premiums, partly offset by receivables; historical OCF/NI ~1.2-1.3x pre-crisis.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 repricing works roughly as guided: MCR settles near 88%, MA margins clear 3% and rebuild toward 4-5% by 2028, and Optum Health stabilises at lower revenue but positive margins after shedding ~1M risk patients. Revenue growth returns to health-spend-plus (6-6.5%) from 2027 as Optum Rx specialty growth and modest MA re-expansion resume, but the pre-crisis 13-16% EPS algorithm holds only for the 2027-28 recovery leg and is not sustained: V28 risk-adjustment, tighter MA coding practices under DOJ scrutiny and PBM transparency rules hold mature margins ~1pp below the FY2017-23 mid-cycle. DOJ and Change Healthcare MDL resolve with a civil payment (in the bridge), no exclusion and no forced divestiture.
scenario_narratives.bull: Q2 2026's 86.7% MCR proves the trend has turned, not seasonal noise: MA margins return to the 5-6% pre-2024 level, Hemsley's cost programme and AI-driven admin productivity lift Optum Insight and UHC operating leverage, and Optum Health's re-underwritten VBC book grows profitably again. Revenue compounds 7-8% for three years on aging-population MA penetration and Optum Rx share, and EBITDA margin returns to ~9% (operating margin ~8.3%), essentially the FY2019-23 level. DOJ settles cheaply; PBM reform is watered down.
scenario_narratives.bear: The DOJ criminal/civil probe ends in a corporate integrity agreement that permanently curbs in-home health-assessment coding and Optum's internal referral economics, PBM delinking legislation passes, and the MA cost trend re-accelerates beyond the 88.1% guide so the recovery stalls in 2027. UNH keeps ceding MA members to protect margin, Optum Health shrinks further, and brand damage from the claims-denial backlash invites more regulation. Revenue grows only 2-4.5% and EBITDA margin stalls at ~6.8% (operating margin ~5.9%), a permanent step down from the integrated-model economics; exit multiple de-rates to 13x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): an open-ended DOJ criminal probe with a single dominant regulator/payer (CMS) and a guidance credibility collapse in 2025 are exactly the single-regulator and unproven-turnaround triggers for a heavier bear weight. Base 50%: two raised FY2026 guides and an 86.7% Q2 MCR make a guided recovery the central case. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs MA margins, Optum Health re-growth and a benign DOJ outcome to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Trough-aware owner-FCF DCF. FY2025 is treated as an underwriting-cycle trough and excluded from margin base rates; value rests on a partial (not full) recovery to a mid-cycle margin haircut for structural MA and PBM regulatory drag. Investment income on the regulated float stays in the flows; only unrestricted cash is credited. NCI and an expected legal cost are deducted once in the bridge. Risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights at a single 8.0% USD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: DOJ criminal/civil MA risk-adjustment probe (expanded to Optum Rx and physician reimbursement): fines, FCA liability, a corporate integrity agreement or, in the tail, program exclusion
MA medical cost trend re-acceleration beyond the 88.1% FY2026 MCR guide stalling the margin recovery
V28 risk-adjustment phase-in and star-ratings pressure capping MA margins below the pre-2024 level
PBM reform (rebate delinking) compressing Optum Rx economics
Change Healthcare MDL liability (uncapped, no settlement), and antitrust action against Optum's vertical integration
Regulated-capital assumption: if a larger share of cash & equivalents is trapped in regulated subsidiaries than assumed, the net-debt credit overstates value by up to ~$30/share
